narrative.text: Defines the category "recommended only in the context of rigorous research", used where there is important uncertainty. It explains that implementation should take the form of research with comparison groups and baseline measures, ideally randomised trials, plus qualitative work where acceptability or feasibility is in doubt.

Defines the "not recommended" category and states that the guideline panel, convened by WHO in Geneva in April and June 2012, made 119 recommendations across eight types of health worker. It notes questions the panel excluded, such as self-administered misoprostol, and the removal of antiretroviral recommendations to align with newer WHO HIV guidance. It stresses the need for national dialogue on implementation and lists recommended tasks by cadre, from health promotion by lay health workers to caesarean section by advanced-level associate clinicians.

The front matter of the Chinese edition of WHO's 2012 recommendations on optimising health worker roles for maternal and newborn health through task shifting, with copyright and disclaimer text. It includes a table defining health worker cadres, such as advanced-level and mid-level associate clinicians, auxiliary nurses, auxiliary midwives and lay health workers, with their training and alternative titles. It then summarises the guideline methods, including GRADE evidence profiles and the DECIDE framework. The block ends by introducing the recommendation categories used by the guideline panel.
